key_insight: Diffusion language models need to know when revision will help—not just which tokens look uncertain. Sudoku experiments show that hidden states reveal errors that token confidence can miss, while regenerating an isolated error often repeats it if its context stays unchanged.
problem_solved: Remasking lets diffusion language models revise generated text, but identifying useful correction opportunities is difficult: confidence can overlook errors, and unchanged surrounding context can reinforce mistakes.
method: Diagnose error signals and remasking behavior using Sudoku.
Compare error information in hidden states with token confidence, and examine whether isolated regeneration corrects mistakes.
Introduce DiVR, a verifier that predicts whether a partially generated sequence will reach a correct answer. The provided abstract is truncated, so training and deployment details are unavailable.
impact: The findings suggest that effective regeneration needs richer signals than token confidence and attention to surrounding context. For practitioners, DiVR offers a direction toward verifier-guided revision, though the excerpt provides no quantitative performance results.
visual_elements: Sudoku grid highlighting an incorrect entry that repeats after isolated remasking.
Side-by-side illustration of token confidence missing an error and hidden-state signals revealing it.
Pipeline diagram: partially generated sequence → DiVR → predicted likelihood of a correct final answer.
Context diagram showing how fixed neighboring tokens can reinforce a regenerated mistake.
paper_title: Learning When Diffusion Language Models Should Regenerate
paper_authors: Minhae Oh, Jeonghye Kim, Jinwoo Koo, Yeongoon Kim, Jimin Seo
